_comment: Hand curation for the phone shelf. 'drop' removes unsorted books that his answers say won't land; 'about' fills in descriptions; 'add' are new books picked for his strongest pulls. Regenerate data.js with tools/build-phone-data.js.
drop: Leyte: The Return to the Philippines
Hurricane: Victor of the Battle of Britain
The Battle of Britain: Five Months That Changed History
The Clay Pigeons of St. Lo
Brothers in Arms: The Epic Story of the 761st Tank Battalion
Okinawa: The Last Battle of World War II

about.bitter-victory-d-este: The Allied invasion of Sicily in July and August 1943, including Patton's race to Messina and his rivalry with Montgomery.
about.clash-of-the-carriers-tillman: The Battle of the Philippine Sea in June 1944, the 'Great Marianas Turkey Shoot,' told largely through the American carrier pilots and aircrews.
about.battle-of-leyte-gulf-cutler: A readable account of the Battle of Leyte Gulf, October 23–26, 1944, from the submarine ambush in Palawan Passage to Halsey's run north and the destroyers' stand off Samar.
about.thousand-mile-war-garfield: The forgotten campaign in Alaska and the Aleutian Islands, from the Japanese landings on Attu and Kiska in 1942 to the bloody American recapture of Attu in 1943.
about.boys-of-pointe-du-hoc-brinkley: The 2nd Ranger Battalion's climb up the cliffs of Pointe du Hoc on D-Day, and Ronald Reagan's 1984 speech honoring the men who made it.
about.battle-for-leyte-gulf-woodward: One of the first full accounts of the Battle of Leyte Gulf, written in 1947 by a historian who had served in the Navy during the war.
about.leyte-morison: Volume 12 of Samuel Eliot Morison's history of the U.S. Navy in WWII: the Leyte landings of October 1944 and the great naval battle that followed.
about.lightning-down-clavin: P-38 pilot Jim Brown, shot down over France in 1944, and his long fight to survive and escape as a prisoner of the Germans.
about.hell-hawks-dorr: The P-47 Thunderbolt pilots of the 365th Fighter Group, flying low-level attack missions in support of the troops from Normandy into Germany.
about.combat-crew-comer: A B-17 flight engineer and gunner's day-by-day account of his 25 missions with the 381st Bomb Group over Europe in 1943.
about.tarawa-the-story-of-a-battle-sherrod: A Time magazine correspondent's eyewitness account of the Marines' landing at Tarawa in November 1943, written within weeks of the battle.
about.mission-beyond-darkness-reed: Air Group 16's long-range strike on the Japanese fleet at the Battle of the Philippine Sea in June 1944, and the pilots' desperate return to their carriers in the dark. Written during the war.
about.tumult-in-the-clouds-goodson: An American who joined the RAF before Pearl Harbor and became a fighter ace with the 4th Fighter Group, flying Spitfires, P-47s and P-51s over Europe.
about.ghost-mountain-boys-campbell: The Army's 32nd Infantry Division marching across New Guinea's Owen Stanley mountains and fighting the brutal battle for Buna in 1942.
about.thunderbolt-johnson: Robert S. Johnson's own story of becoming one of the top American fighter aces over Europe, flying the P-47 with the 56th Fighter Group.
about.rock-of-anzio-whitlock: The 45th Infantry Division's war from Sicily through Salerno, Anzio and southern France to the liberation of Dachau.
about.yeager-yeager: Chuck Yeager's autobiography: P-51 ace over Europe, shot down and escaped through France, then the test pilot who broke the sound barrier.
about.fatal-decision-d-este: The Anzio landing of January 1944 and the four-month fight to hold the beachhead and break out toward Rome.
about.torpedo-junction-hickam: The U-boat attacks off North Carolina's Outer Banks in 1942, and the Coast Guard and Navy crews who fought back.
about.d-day-the-battle-for-normandy-beevor: The Normandy campaign from the D-Day landings through the breakout and the closing of the Falaise Pocket in August 1944.
about.little-ship-big-war-the-saga-of-de343-st: The destroyer escort USS Abercrombie and her crew, from the Leyte landings through the kamikaze attacks off Okinawa, told by an officer who served aboard.
about.when-the-sea-came-alive-graff: D-Day told in the words of the people who lived it, stitched together from hundreds of first-hand accounts, from the planners to the men on the beaches.
about.queen-of-the-flat-tops-johnston: A war correspondent aboard the carrier USS Lexington describes her fights in early 1942 and her loss at the Battle of the Coral Sea. Published in 1942.
about.clear-the-bridge-o-kane: The war patrols of the submarine USS Tang, told by her captain, Richard O'Kane, from her record-setting sinkings to her loss in October 1944.
about.red-blood-black-sand-tatum: A young Marine machine gunner's memoir of Iwo Jima, where he fought beside Medal of Honor recipient John Basilone.
about.they-were-expendable-white: The PT boat crews who fought in the Philippines in 1941–42 and carried MacArthur out of Corregidor. Published in 1942.
about.bridge-at-remagen-hechler: How the 9th Armored Division captured the Ludendorff Bridge over the Rhine intact in March 1945, by an Army historian who interviewed the men soon after.
about.thunder-below-fluckey: Eugene Fluckey's account of commanding the submarine USS Barb, which raided Japanese convoys and even sent a landing party ashore to blow up a train.
about.night-drop-marshall: The American airborne landings in Normandy on D-Day night, built from interviews S. L. A. Marshall conducted with paratroopers right after the battle.
about.wahoo-o-kane: Richard O'Kane's account of serving as executive officer on the submarine USS Wahoo under Dudley 'Mush' Morton, one of the boldest skippers of the war.
about.most-dangerous-enemy-bungay: A complete history of the Battle of Britain in 1940, covering the pilots, the radar network and the commanders on both sides.
about.no-better-place-to-die-murphy: The 82nd Airborne's fight for the La Fière causeway over the Merderet River in the first days after D-Day.
about.fighter-the-true-story-of-the-battle-of-: Len Deighton's history of the Battle of Britain, strong on the aircraft, the tactics and the pilots flying them.
about.dog-company-o-donnell: The Rangers of Dog Company, 2nd Ranger Battalion, from the cliffs of Pointe du Hoc on D-Day to Hill 400 in the Hürtgen Forest.
about.first-light-wellum: A teenage RAF Spitfire pilot's memoir of flying in the Battle of Britain.

add.title: For Crew and Country
add.author: John Wukovits
add.about: The destroyer escort USS Samuel B. Roberts and her crew, from her commissioning to her charge against Japanese battleships off Samar in October 1944.

add.title: Tin Can Titans
add.author: John Wukovits
add.about: The ships and crews of the most decorated U.S. Navy destroyer squadron of WWII, from the Solomon Islands battles to the end of the Pacific war.

add.title: Dogfight over Tokyo
add.author: John Wukovits
add.about: The carrier pilots of Fighting Squadron 88 and their air battle over Tokyo on August 15, 1945, the morning Japan surrendered.

add.title: American Commando
add.author: John Wukovits
add.about: Evans Carlson and his Marine Raiders, from the raid on Makin Island to their long patrol behind Japanese lines.

add.title: Destroyer Squadron 23
add.author: Ken Jones
add.about: Arleigh Burke's 'Little Beavers' destroyer squadron in the Solomon Islands in 1943, including the Battle of Cape St. George.

add.title: Battleship at War
add.author: Ivan Musicant
add.about: The battleship USS Washington, from Atlantic convoy duty to her night duel that sank the Japanese battleship Kirishima in November 1942, and on through the Pacific war.

add.title: D-Day in the Pacific: The Battle of Saipan
add.author: Harold J. Goldberg
add.about: The June–July 1944 invasion of Saipan by Marines and Army troops, told through the men who fought it.

add.title: The Hero of Hacksaw Ridge
add.author: Booton Herndon
add.about: Desmond Doss, the unarmed Army medic who saved dozens of wounded men on the Maeda Escarpment at Okinawa and received the Medal of Honor. First published as The Unlikeliest Hero.

add.title: Darby's Rangers: We Led the Way
add.author: William O. Darby & William H. Baumer
add.about: The Ranger battalions' war in North Africa, Sicily and Italy, told by their founder, William Darby, who was killed in action in 1945.

add.title: The Devil's Brigade
add.author: Robert H. Adleman & George Walton
add.about: The First Special Service Force, the joint American-Canadian commando unit, from training in Montana through Monte la Difensa and Anzio. The basis for the 1968 film.

add.title: Anzio: Italy and the Battle for Rome
add.author: Lloyd Clark
add.about: The Anzio landing of January 1944 and the costly fight for the beachhead, told from soldiers' accounts on both sides.

add.title: Big Week
add.author: James Holland
add.about: The week in February 1944 when American bombers and fighters set out to break the Luftwaffe over Germany, told through the crews on both sides.

add.title: The Americans at D-Day
add.author: John C. McManus
add.about: The American soldiers, sailors and airmen of June 6, 1944, from the airborne drops behind the beaches to the landings at Utah and Omaha.

add.title: Beyond the Beachhead
add.author: Joseph Balkoski
add.about: The 29th Infantry Division in Normandy, from Omaha Beach through the hedgerow battles to the capture of St. Lô.
